### `unferprotocolboardBoardKindeffectkind`.

> G1: the shared context board — typed, append-only, sanitized, bounded. A projection over the same cursor space as `events_poll`, so one checkpoint covers both. `board_write` is Observe-kind for OBSERVED/FACT/FAIL and Mutate-kind for CLAIM/ESCALATE/PATCH_SUMMARY, per `unfer_protocol::board::BoardKind::effect_kind`.

- `board_write`

### ungrouped

- `board_read`
- `board_grep`

### workers cannot settle it among themselves.

> G3: claims with overlap detection, direct messages between workers, and the explicit escalation to the human lane. `agent_claim` reports an overlap rather than refusing it — see `unfer_protocol::coop` for why a board cannot arbitrate — and `agent_escalate` is what happens when the workers cannot settle it among themselves.

- `agent_claim`

### ungrouped

- `agent_dm`
- `agent_dm_read`
- `agent_escalate`

### the hand-off is observable after the fact.

> G7: role hand-off. Carries no privilege; it records who is reviewing so the hand-off is observable after the fact.

- `agent_handoff`

### a conflict approves nothing). See `mathedcoresync`.

> G5: write-time conflict detection. `sync_edit` records this document's own footprint; `sync_import` classifies a peer's packet against it and routes an overlap to the board as a FAIL entry (Observe-kind — recording a conflict approves nothing). See `mathed_core::sync`.

### workers last change. See `unferprotocolevidence`.

> G4: verify-before-merge. `gate_record` registers a run of a gate that already exists; `patch_submit` writes a PATCH_SUMMARY that cites one, and is refused when the citation is unknown, non-green, or older than the worker's last change. See `unfer_protocol::evidence`.

- `gate_record`

> D5: the analytic decision engine. `observe`-kind only — there is no `Mutate` arm for any of these, because the engine is advice and must never be able to approve, merge, gate, sign or certify. See `unfer_protocol::decide`.
